resolved_items.resolution: The K=3 source-derivation boundary is resolvable from earlier results in the same PDF. At overall K=3, Algorithm 5.10 calls SumK(r,2), which the paper identifies with Sum2. Proposition 4.5, equivalently Lemma 4.9(ii) with SumK parameter 2, gives |res-s|<=eps|s|+gamma_(2N-1)^2 S for the length-2N vector r. Combining equation (5.3), S<=|d|+gamma_(2N)A, with monotonicity of gamma under 8N eps<=1 gives a bound no larger than (eps+2 gamma_(4N-2)^2)|d|+gamma_(4N-2)^3 A. Thus Proposition 5.11's K=3 statement is justified even though its displayed derivation invokes Proposition 4.10 outside that proposition's printed parameter range. The source's other listed ambiguities do not affect the selected absolute result: the nonzero condition belongs only to the relative bound; later addition underflow is covered by exact TwoSum; and the behavioral contracts suffice for the paper's finite real-valued executions.

Global structure axioms do not reduce paper applicability because every concrete selected execution admits an exact off-run extension. resolved_items.primary_evidence: PDF p. 5 explicitly says IEEE 754 is unnecessary when the error-free transformations are available, while PDF p. 8 records the properties needed by the analysis. The Lean structures D010, D014, and D017 axiomatize those properties over Real. Besides the exact u=0 model, a positive-u non-IEEE instance exists for 0<u<=1/8 by taking fl_add(a,b)=b when a=0 and (a+b)(1+u) otherwise, twoSum=(fl_add,a+b-fl_add), and twoProduct=(ab,0); it satisfies the declaration fields and hsmall at N=1.

resolved_items.resolution: Lean reverses Algorithm 4.3's written TwoSum operands during repeated VecSum passes, but the paper specialization computes identical ordered output pairs. For finite real-valued paper operands, both orders have the same rounded high fl(a+b), and exactness uniquely fixes the low as a+b-high. The initial DotK transformation itself already uses running-high first in both Algorithm 5.10 and Lean. Order-sensitive abstract models therefore add scope but do not change the paper specialization.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: PDF p. 11 writes [p_i,p_(i-1)]=TwoSum(p_i,p_(i-1)); PDF p. 23 writes [p,r_(N+i-1)]=TwoSum(p,h). PDF p. 8, Theorem 3.4, states high=fl(a+b) and high+low=a+b. Declaration D026 folds as twoSum(running,next), and D012 applies that same transform to the product highs.

lean_implies_paper.reasoning: For paper dimension N set Lean n=N-1 and u=eps. Extend each concrete no-underflow execution's reached operations to an ErrorFreeDotModel using exact off-run behavior. The paper's equations (2.1)-(2.3) and Theorem 3.4 discharge every model field, and operand-order symmetry makes Lean's VecSum numerically identical on the paper specialization. Unfolding D005-D013 then reproduces Algorithm 5.10, its SumK(r,K-1) call, exact dot product, magnitude, gamma index, and selected inequality, including K=3 via Proposition 4.5.

paper_implies_lean.reasoning: The paper result is restricted to working-precision vectors and its concrete arithmetic execution. It does not assert the bound for arbitrary real vectors or every total abstract model satisfying D010, D014, and D017, including exact and order-sensitive non-IEEE models admitted by Lean.

rationale: Primary inspection of PDF pp. 5-8, 11, 15-16, 20, and 23-24 and declarations D001-D102 resolves the disagreement. N=n+1 is an exact positive-dimension reindexing; the transformed vector, SumK parameter, exact reference value, magnitude, gamma index, coefficients, powers, and non-strict absolute inequality match. A finite reached-operation extension embeds every selected no-underflow paper run into the global Lean model. The apparent VecSum operand reversal is observationally identical for the paper's TwoSum, and the K=3 boundary follows from the paper's Sum2 estimate even though the local derivation cites Proposition 4.10 too broadly. Lean retains all paper cases and has satisfiable extra real-domain and abstract-model cases, so the final classification is faithful-stronger.
